Description: Paired conjoint on news sources in the Norwegian Citizen Panel (1,955 respondents, one task each): two hypothetical sources described by advertising, which party the editor/owner openly supports, press-ethics violations, comment field, readership, publication form, entertainment content and when founded; the respondent chose one. The article presents it as a trust study, but the deposit does not contain the question stem.
Reference: Knudsen, E., & Johannesson, M. P. (2019). Beyond the limits of survey experiments: How conjoint designs advance causal inference in political communication research. Political Communication, 36(2), 259-271.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/knudsen_2019.R. The deposit ships PREPARED data only: its README says the raw Norwegian Citizen Panel file cannot be shared under data-protection law, and the CC0 covers the prepared files. Question stem not recoverable (no codebook or instrument in the deposit; NCP wave 8/9 codebook not public). Respondents saw Norwegian; level text is the deposit English, verbatim including Online newpaper (sic). id is the authors 1..1955 re-keying, not the panel id. The deposits selective-exposure file is held: pick-2-of-4, and headlines drawn from a pool of 755 real articles.

Description: Paired candidate-choice conjoint in the Norwegian Citizen Panel (1,139 respondents, three tasks each): two hypothetical members of parliament described by age, gender, region, relationship, education, religion and work, plus their positions on income inequality, refugees social rights and where emission cuts should be made. A within-respondent manipulation showed only the social characteristics, only the issue positions, or both.
Reference: Arnesen, S., Duell, D., & Johannesson, M. P. (2019). Do citizens make inferences from political candidate characteristics when aiming for substantive representation? Electoral Studies, 57, 46-60.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/arnesen_2019_representation.R. The deposit ships PREPARED data only: its README says the raw Norwegian Citizen Panel file cannot be shared under data-protection law, and the CC0 covers the prepared files. Hidden attributes are the reserved (not shown), verified structural. Respondents saw Norwegian; level text is the authors English translation. cov_vote_intent is vote choice, not party identification. id is the panel respondent id, so it links to arnesen_2019_attitude_prediction and arnesen_2019_referendum_mandate.

Description: Paired conjoint in the Norwegian Citizen Panel (1,077 respondents, three tasks each): two hypothetical people described by age, gender, region, relationship, education, religion and work, with the respondent picking which would agree with a stated political attitude. Whether the pair was presented as ordinary persons or as politicians varied between respondents.
Reference: Arnesen, S., Duell, D., & Johannesson, M. P. (2019). Do citizens make inferences from political candidate characteristics when aiming for substantive representation? Electoral Studies, 57, 46-60.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/arnesen_2019_representation.R. The deposit ships PREPARED data only (see the sibling table). The outcome picks among the profiles, so it is a choice and not a rating; the attitude is trial_attitude. The display order is not recorded in this experiment, so task indexes the attitude. Respondents saw Norwegian; level text is the authors English translation. cov_vote_intent is vote choice, not party identification.

Description: Factorial survey in the Norwegian Citizen Panel (1,065 respondents, one vignette each): a Norwegian sentence about a hypothetical advisory referendum on EU membership, varying turnout, the winning sides share of the vote and which side won, each of which could also be withheld. Respondents said whether the government must act on the result even if parliament disagreed.
Reference: Arnesen, S., Broderstad, T. S., Johannesson, M. P., & Linde, J. (2019). Conditional legitimacy: How turnout, majority size, and outcome affect perceptions of legitimacy in European Union membership referendums. European Union Politics, 20(2), 176-197.
Notes: Script data/conjoint/arnesen_2019_referendum.R. The deposit ships PREPARED data only: its README says the raw Norwegian Citizen Panel wave 7 file cannot be shared under data-protection law, and the CC0 covers the prepared file. LEVELS ARE NOT EQUIPROBABLE: the 60-cell design is enumerated as 144 lottery tickets spread unevenly, and selection is uniform over tickets, so the withheld states are over-sampled by construction (turnout not shown in 50 percent of rows against 12 percent per disclosed level). opt_out yes: 248 of 1,065 said no. cov_age_group comes from a column named rsp_age that is bands, not years. id is the panel respondent id and links to the two arnesen_2019 representation tables.
